# Migrax

> Migrax generates SQL migrations from JPA/Hibernate entities and applies them, with locking, checksums, rollback scripts, linting and verification. It runs as a command line tool, a Maven or Gradle plugin, a container image, and at startup in Spring Boot, Quarkus, Micronaut and Helidon, on PostgreSQL, CockroachDB, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle, H2 and SQLite.

Full text of every page: https://migrax.org/llms-full.txt

## Overview
- [Home](https://migrax.org/): What Migrax is, a short example, and how to get started.
- [Download](https://migrax.org/download/): Migrax needs Java 17 or newer. Download the command line tool below, then run its installer as described in Installation.

## Getting started
- [Installation](https://migrax.org/getting-started/installation/): Migrax is a command line tool. It needs Java 17 or newer; nothing else has to be installed, and no administrator rights are needed.
- [Quick start](https://migrax.org/getting-started/quickstart/): This takes about five minutes. You need a service with JPA entities, a `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`, and a database it can reach.

## Guides: Everyday use
- [How Migrax works](https://migrax.org/guides/how-it-works/): Entities are read into a schema model, compared with the snapshot, and the difference becomes a migration file with a rollback script; migrax migrate applies it to the database and records it in migrax_history.
- [Changing entities](https://migrax.org/guides/changing-entities/): The everyday loop is short:
- [Rollbacks and recovery](https://migrax.org/guides/rollbacks-and-recovery/): Every generated migration has a rollback script in `rollback/<same name>.sql`.
- [Advanced migrations](https://migrax.org/guides/advanced-migrations/): Some data changes are easier in Java than in SQL.

## Guides: Teams and CI
- [Working in a team](https://migrax.org/guides/team-workflow/): The snapshot is written with one table, column, index and key per line, so git can merge changes two people made to different tables.
- [Continuous integration](https://migrax.org/guides/ci/): Three commands make a good CI gate:
- [Comparing databases](https://migrax.org/guides/comparing-databases/): New in Migrax 0.14.0.
- [Java API and JUnit tests](https://migrax.org/guides/java-api-and-tests/): New in Migrax 0.10.0.

## Guides: Production
- [Production safety](https://migrax.org/guides/production-safety/): Migrax is built around one idea: a migration should be proven before it runs in production.
- [Zero-downtime changes](https://migrax.org/guides/zero-downtime/): New in Migrax 0.11.0.
- [Metrics and tracing](https://migrax.org/guides/observability/): New in Migrax 0.13.0.
- [Containers and Kubernetes](https://migrax.org/guides/containers-and-kubernetes/): In container platforms, migrations usually run as their own step before the new version of the application starts: a Kubernetes Job, an init container, or a deploy hook.

## Guides: Other setups
- [Several databases](https://migrax.org/guides/several-databases/): New in Migrax 0.15.0.
- [Switching from Flyway or Liquibase](https://migrax.org/guides/switching-tools/): A project that already manages its database with Flyway or Liquibase can move to Migrax with one command, without running anything again on the database.
- [SQL migrations for any language](https://migrax.org/guides/sql-migrations-for-any-language/): Migrax applies SQL migrations you write yourself, in any project: Python, Node.js, Go, .NET, PHP, Ruby, or a Java application without JPA.
- [Schema file from your ORM](https://migrax.org/guides/schema-from-orm/): New in Migrax 0.17.0.
- [Using Migrax with AI assistants](https://migrax.org/guides/ai-assistants/): AI coding assistants can use Migrax directly: they read what changed, preview the SQL with its risks, and explain it to you, while you stay the one who changes the database.

## Frameworks
- [Frameworks and build tools](https://migrax.org/frameworks/): Migrax doesn't depend on any framework, or on Java.
- [Spring Boot](https://migrax.org/frameworks/spring-boot/): Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:
- [Quarkus](https://migrax.org/frameworks/quarkus/): Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:
- [Micronaut](https://migrax.org/frameworks/micronaut/): Micronaut 4 and 5 are supported.
- [Helidon](https://migrax.org/frameworks/helidon/): Migrax comes in two parts, and most projects use both:
- [Jakarta EE and plain Hibernate](https://migrax.org/frameworks/jakarta-ee/): Any project with JPA entities works, with or without an application framework.
- [Any language](https://migrax.org/frameworks/any-language/): Migrax isn't only for Java. Any application that keeps its database changes as SQL files can use it to apply them: Python, Node.js, Go, .NET, PHP, Ruby or anything else.
- [Maven plugin](https://migrax.org/frameworks/maven/): Everything the command line does is also available as Maven goals, which is handy in CI or when you prefer not to install the CLI.
- [Gradle plugin](https://migrax.org/frameworks/gradle/): repositories { mavenCentral() // the plugin loads the Migrax library from here }
- [IntelliJ IDEA plugin](https://migrax.org/intellij/): The Migrax plugin brings Migrax into IntelliJ IDEA: a tool window with the state of every migration, buttons for the everyday commands, an icon next to entity classes whose changes are not in a migration yet, and lint...

## Reference
- [CLI commands](https://migrax.org/reference/cli/): Run `migrax help <command>` for the same information in the terminal.
- [Configuration](https://migrax.org/reference/configuration/): Most projects need no configuration: Migrax reads the settings your application already has.
- [Naming strategies](https://migrax.org/reference/naming/): Hibernate turns entity and field names into table and column names, and each framework configures that differently.
- [Databases](https://migrax.org/reference/databases/): The dialect comes from the JDBC URL. When there is no database URL (for example in a CI step that only plans), pass `--dialect`.
- [Entity readers](https://migrax.org/reference/hibernate/): With Hibernate 4 or newer in your project, Migrax asks your Hibernate version itself for the mapping, without connecting to a database.
- [Lint rules](https://migrax.org/reference/lint-rules/): Migrax lints every migration it generates, and `migrax lint` checks pending migrations (or `--all`, or named files).
- [Errors and JSON output](https://migrax.org/reference/errors-and-json/): Every command can report its result as JSON with `--json`, and every error has a stable code.
- [Troubleshooting](https://migrax.org/reference/troubleshooting/): Start with `migrax doctor`: it checks Java, the build, the entities, the database connection and risky settings, and says how to fix each problem.
- [Limitations](https://migrax.org/reference/limitations/): What Migrax doesn't do yet, and what to do instead.

## Project
- [Versioning and releases](https://migrax.org/project/versioning/): Migrax versions follow Semantic Versioning: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.
- [Contributing to Migrax](https://migrax.org/project/contributing/): Thank you for helping. This guide covers building, testing and the rules for branches, commits and releases.
- [Changelog](https://migrax.org/project/changelog/): All notable changes to Migrax are listed here.
- [Privacy](https://migrax.org/project/privacy/): This page covers the website migrax.org.
